# Colony chronicle — seed 1, 100 years

Generated by `game/tools/chronicle.gd` on the full simulation (economy, companies, law, staff, politics). The player's party (Founders') runs on autoplay. Month m0 = January, Year 1; parties form in Year 3; elections every 4 years plus any extra elections.

Contents: 1 Summary · 2 Parties (why each appeared) · 3 Governments · 4 Elections (campaign and every voter group) · 5 Bills and decisions · 6 Lever changes · 7 Year-by-year condition · 8 Event log · 9 Unions, trade, industry and the press

## What changed since the last chronicles (v5), and what is still to come

These chronicles (v6, seeds 1–3) ran on the working build of 2026-11-13, 15:20. They include Bob's new population
model and the housing life-cycle, still being tuned; the consumer-industry fix comes in v7.

### Changed since v5

**Population: ages, booms and a retirement wave (Bob, E120)**
- People are tracked in 5-year age bands. The founders are mostly 20–40, so there is a baby boom in the first years
  and an echo boom a generation later.
- Births follow age, falling with income, education, density and crowding. Deaths follow age, health care, crowding
  and famine.
- Retirement now takes people who are in work, so the founding generation retires as a wave (around Years 25–50),
  opening jobs and raising pensions.
- **Migration** = the home world's ship space × the colony's attractiveness (wages, jobs, food, housing, safety)
  × the new **immigration law** (one policy, 0 closed to 100 open; parliament can change it). Young adults with no
  job can emigrate.
- People who left the workforce come back when there are jobs.
- Shortages of homes show as crowding and slums (above 120% occupancy), not as a hidden cap.

**Housing ages and needs work (Bob, S3 — your decision A37)**
- Homes barely age for 20 years, then decay fast, more slowly if maintained.
- Every quarter, owners of run-down blocks decide: the state housing office renovates if the budget allows,
  landlords if they can pay 30% and borrow the rest; otherwise the block slides toward a slum.
- Renovations are real construction work. Rents follow condition.
- Private developers build with 10% equity and a loan. A housing company is founded from private savings if no firm
  can. A failed landlord's homes pass to the state housing office, so nobody is evicted.
- Governments plan housing ahead using a population forecast: state-minded governments look up to 3 years ahead and
  build; market-minded ones offer developers a grant.

**Politics and the v5 review**
- **Confidence-and-supply prices** are on the government's agenda first; they pass the fiscal guard and the bill
  memory (tested directly).
- **No endless tinkering**: moving the same law again the same way costs a government more, unless it is its
  programme.
- **Union endorsements**: coalition partners are judged together, so a union can't hop to a partner that voted the
  same cut (the v5 "four switches in one month" bug).
- **Merged parties** carry their cabinet, PM and support roles to the absorbing party.
- **Hot issues** (Ella): campaigns and debates draw on the issues voters are talking about.
- **The home world claims an export levy** when the colony's trade is rich and it is needy, and can reserve the top
  export for its own buyer.
- **Depots**: governments build one when the port keeps filling before the ships come.

**Economy and society**
- **Exports**: only real producers export (builders and co-ops no longer "exported" their input stock). Colony
  Power & Water really is the top exporter: the state took over the mines, smelters and works in rescues.
- **Professionals' Association** now has a grievance: professional pay falling behind ordinary wages.
- **Worker co-ops** rescue a failing plant at most once every 5 years (seed 3's 628 insolvencies were co-op chains).
- **Newspapers** manage their money (price, investigations, staff), so papers last for decades; fewer, better-founded
  exposures of false reports.
- **Laws**: immigration; essential-services strikes; trade, transport and union laws.

**Not visible in this text, but in the game**
- **The office**: your newspaper, reports, inbox from named staff, calls, calendar, visitors and hiring interviews —
  as tabs, a drawn desk, or a 3D office (placeholder shapes until your asset pack is in), with a real window view of
  the colony through the seasons and weather.
- **Roads and bridges** on the colony map; tourist sites; waste sites and river pollution on the map.
- **Choosing the world** for the expedition (the start of A47).

### What this run shows (seed 1)
- **Adults**: 1,537 at Year 1, peak 3,307 (Year 74), 2,995 at Year 100.
- **Unemployment** averages 19.7% (range 4.8–54.4%); **real income** averages 154 and ends at 138.
- **Famine** in Year(s) 20.
- **Strikes**: 21 over the century.
- **Exports**: 44.5 million credits in 48 ships.
- **Housing**: 16 blocks fell into disrepair, 1 were renovated.
- **Immigration law** changes: 70→90, 90→70, 70→50, 50→30, 30→10, 10→0.
- Parties that ever existed: 19 (active at the end: 9); Elections: 25.

### Known problems in this build
- **Housing froze — a bug, not politics.** Bob's check on this exact build: about 1,150 homes from Year 10
  onward and every district an overcrowded slum (140–175% occupancy) for most of the century. The cause, found during
  this run: a housing block is the biggest project in the game and no builder can finish it inside the 12-month
  bidding window, so nobody bids — government orders and developers' projects sat untouched. Parliament then closed
  immigration (70 → 30 → 0) because of crowding and joblessness, and the boom stalled. Read the housing and
  immigration history in this run as the effect of that bug.
  **Fix ready for v7**: a 24-month window for housing; developers trying the next district; new builders founded
  when housing tenders sit unbid; and big projects tendered in **lots** that several builders share (consortia
  allowed), placed outward in phases that can found new quarters and redraw districts (your idea).
- **Population** therefore peaks around 4,000–5,000 adults and people instead of your 6,000–15,000 target.
- **Consumer workshops** still don't take hold (a failing test in this build: no workshop appears in 72 months on the
  economy-only seed); the fix is the v7 item above.
- Two tests failed in this working build (consumer workshops; a hot-issues housing question) — both are in-progress
  work by Bob and Ella and will be fixed before v7.


### Still to come
- **The consumer-industry fix** (v5 review P0): workshops that take hold instead of service hubs; shortages sent to
  the government first, which can offer grants, build, or authorise imports; a cheap home-made fallback.
- **The economy on areas and emergent settlements** (A46): the colony starts as the landing camp; the founding years
  as the guided introduction; villages that grow into towns and decline.
- **The expedition** (A47): planet, colonists, cargo and investors with real costs; the charter; the first bank.
- **Banking**: deposits, mortgages and home ownership, interest-rate politics, bank failures.
- **Sister colonies** (A48): 3–6 neighbours, trade and diplomacy months apart, a League, joint independence.
- **Transport**: freight by route, buses and commuting, tour operators with rovers and airships, traffic and
  engineers' reports.
- **Waste, sewage and the dead** (A45); leisure and tourists; colonial goods; technology later.
